key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the CAG Report had persuasive value but not finality, and that the CBI's reliance on it was misplaced. The Court also accepted that the coal rejects did not have any useful calorific value, as per the CIMFR Washability Report.
witness_credibility: The Court assessed that the Sanctioning Authority, namely the Board of Directors of KPCL, thoroughly scrutinized all relevant documents and depositions of 67 witnesses submitted by the CBI, and found no evidence of criminal intent.

legal_representation.accused: Ranjit Kumar, Sr. Adv., Abhimanyu Bhandari, Ms. Rooh-e-hina Dua, Ayush Aggarwal, Sangram S. Saron, Arav Pandit, Advs.
legal_representation.state: R.S. Cheema, Sr. Adv., Ms. Tarannum Cheema, Akshay Nagrajan, Akash Singh, Mukesh Kumar Maroria, Advs.

investigation_status: CBI conducted an investigation based on the Audit Report of the CAG, but the Supreme Court found the investigation to be flawed and unsustainable
procedural_irregularity: The CBI's investigation was found to be a 'roving and fishing inquiry' based on the Audit Report of the CAG, which had not attained finality

appeal_history.trial_court: Order on Charge dated 24.12.2021 and Order framing Charges dated 03.03.2022
appeal_history.high_court: The High Court's decision dated 24.03.2016 was upheld by the Supreme Court on 20.05.2022
appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeals allowed, orders quashed and set aside

prosecution_argument: The respondent-CBI relied on the Audit Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) to launch prosecution against the appellants, asserting that the report had the seal of approval of the Parliament and had attained finality. The CBI also argued that the coal rejects had useful calorific value making them saleable commodities and that the appellants were responsible for not setting up a coal washery at the pithead.
defence_argument: The appellants argued that the CAG Report could not form the basis for launching proceedings against them as it had not attained finality and was merely persuasive. They also contended that the coal rejects did not have any useful calorific value, that they were not required to account for the rejects, and that the CBI's investigation was based on misinterpretation of the agreements and the CAG Report.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the material produced by the accused should lead to a conclusion that their defence is based on sound, reasonable and indubitable facts, and that the court must be fully satisfied that the material would persuade a reasonable person to dismiss the accusations as false.
precedent_relied_upon: KPCL v. Aryan Energy Private Limited and Others, COMAP No. 12, 13, 14 and 15 and 2020 decided on 22nd July, 2021; State of Karnataka v. L. Munniswamy [1977] 3 SCR 113 : (1977) 2 SCC 699; State of Tamil Nadu v. N. Suresh Rajan and Others [2014] 1 SCR 135 : (2014) 11 SCC 709; and others as cited in the judgment.
